verifications.claim: Annual flu shots are recommended for everyone 6 months and older.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "It is recommended that everyone 6 months and older get a flu vaccine every season"; "Most people 6 months and older should get a flu shot"; "CDC recommends everyone 6 months and older receive an annual influenza (flu) vaccine"; "everyone 6 months and older get the flu vaccine"; "Everyone ages 6 months and up should get an annual flu vaccine"
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state CDC recommendation for everyone 6 months and older annually.

verifications.claim: Flu shots are ideally administered in September or October to allow two weeks for immunity to build.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "It’s generally recommended that people get a flu vaccine by the end of October"; "It takes about 2 weeks after receiving a flu shot... to build the antibodies"; "it's usually best... to get the flu vaccine in September or October. ... It takes up to two weeks to build immunity"
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly recommend September/October timing due to 2-week immunity build.

verifications.claim: Flu vaccines prevent influenza infection.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "The flu vaccine may reduce flu illnesses"; "they may not always prevent infection"; "provide protection against infection"; "may not always be 100% effective"; "doesn't always provide total protection"
verifications.reasoning: Sources indicate protection and risk reduction but not absolute prevention; claim is overly absolute.

verifications.claim: Flu vaccines reduce symptom severity.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "getting the flu shot may help reduce the severity of illness if you do become sick"; "your vaccination will likely help you become less ill"; "lower the risk of having serious illness from the flu"
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements confirm reduction in severity even if infected.

verifications.claim: Flu vaccines protect against circulating strains.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the vaccine may help protect against the viruses that may be most common during the upcoming flu season"; "protects against the influenza viruses that research suggests will be most common during the upcoming season"
verifications.reasoning: Sources state vaccines target expected circulating strains.
